meta.title: Hyderabad birth certificate (copy of a registered birth) grid-only evidence ledger
meta.disclaimer: Independent research, not official advice. Grid-only benchmark run: sources and claims only, no nodes, edges, roadblocks or journeys. Desk research, no counter visited. Limitations: the corporation's Citizen's Charter, still published on its live homepage, states on its face that it was prepared on 10 May 2013 and would be revised on or before 13 May 2014, so every claim taken from it is graded C and its figures are twelve years past the revision date the document set for itself; the corporation's current birth and death page gives a MeeSeva fee of Rs. 45 while that charter gives Rs. 20 per certificate; the audit held these to be one fact told twice under protocol section 1, cross-linked them, and resolved the conflict against the older figure, so the Rs. 20 claim is contested and supports no cell; the printable application form's file metadata dates it to 2010; the certificate search route was read but never queried with an acknowledgement or application number, and the birth and death login is behind a password and an OTP that were not crossed. Do not submit personal data through this ledger.

scenarios.label: Hyderabad birth certificate copy
scenarios.summary: A parent resident in Hyderabad seeks a certified copy or first certificate of a birth already registered in the city's civil register, by the municipal civil-registration route, public entry, online where offered and counter route otherwise. Delayed registration, name inclusion, corrections, births outside the city and hospital-side registration steps are excluded.

sources.title: Birth and Death - Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation
sources.notes: Jurisdiction: Hyderabad, Telangana, India. Agency naming as displayed on the access date: 'Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation', with the footer reading 'Content owned, maintained and updated by Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation, Government of Telangana' and a copyright line of 2024. The page shows no visible last-updated date. Archive: an existing Wayback snapshot was found at https://web.archive.org/web/20250321142610/https://ghmc.gov.in/Birth.aspx (2025-03-21); no new capture was pushed from this run.

sources.title: Citizen's Charter - Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation
sources.notes: Jurisdiction: Hyderabad, Telangana, India. Agency naming as displayed on the access date: 'Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation'. Twelve pages, linked from the corporation's live homepage menu. The document states of itself: 'This Citizen's Charter has been prepared by the Department on 10th May 2013 and this will be revised on or before 13th May 2014', and is signed for the Principal Secretary to Government (MA). The 2013 preparation date is recorded as publishedAt, and every claim drawn from it is graded C as visibly outdated official material, since the document is twelve years past the revision date it set for itself. Archive: an existing Wayback snapshot was found at https://web.archive.org/web/20260420030903/https://ghmc.gov.in/Menu_Files/citizen-charter-19-06_compress.pdf (2026-04-20); no new capture was pushed from this run.

sources.title: Application for Birth Certificate - Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation
sources.notes: Jurisdiction: Hyderabad, Telangana, India. Agency naming as displayed on the access date: the file is served from the corporation's own CSC_Applications directory and its footer fields refer to a CSC transaction number and date. One page. It carries no visible date on its face; the PDF metadata records a creation date of 2010-04-02, recorded as publishedAt and carried as a stated limitation. Claims from it are graded B as an observed current official form under protocol section 4, the form being the one the corporation currently serves for this service and having been directly observed on the access date; the earlier Grade C reading was corrected on audit under pre-audit lint item 4. It was read only: nothing was filled in or submitted. Archive: an existing Wayback snapshot was found at https://web.archive.org/web/20260517060637/https://ghmc.gov.in/CSC_Applications/BIRTHREQAPP.pdf (2026-05-17); no new capture was pushed from this run.

sources.title: Birth Certificate search by acknowledgement or application number - GHMC births and deaths portal
sources.notes: Jurisdiction: Hyderabad, Telangana, India. Agency naming as displayed on the access date: 'GHMC', with the page footer crediting the Centre for Good Governance and a copyright line of 2024. Direct current observation of a public official interface reachable without login, offering a single field labelled 'Acknowledgement/Application Number' and a Search action. The route was read only: no number was entered and no case data was retrieved. Archive: an existing Wayback snapshot was found at https://web.archive.org/web/20240529160204/https://bnd.ghmc.gov.in/Birth_Certificate.aspx (2024-05-29); no new capture was pushed from this run.

sources.title: Birth certificate output template, issued under section 12/17 - GHMC births and deaths portal
sources.notes: Jurisdiction: Hyderabad, Telangana, India. Agency naming as displayed on the access date: 'GREATER HYDERABAD MUNICIPAL CORPORATION'. Direct current observation of the certificate layout the portal produces, headed 'BIRTH CERTIFICATE (Issued Under Section 12/17)' and reciting that the information is taken from the original record of birth which is the register for a named ward and circle of the corporation. No case data was retrieved; only the empty template's own wording was read. Archive: an existing Wayback snapshot was found at https://web.archive.org/web/20230428161006/https://bnd.ghmc.gov.in/Birth_Certificate_Download.aspx (2023-04-28); no new capture was pushed from this run.

claims.text: The corporation's birth and death page states that for a certificate the citizen approaches any Mee-Seva centre, pays a fee of Rs. 45 and has the certificate dispatched through Mee-Seva to the applicant.
claims.notes: An amount the citizen pays for a certificate, from the corporation's current page, directly observed. The corporation's 2013 Citizen's Charter gives Rs. 20 for the same output; neither source states that it prices a channel to the exclusion of the other, so the two are cross-linked as contradictory under protocol section 1 rather than treated as separate routes. This claim is the stronger evidence, being current, Grade B and observed on the corporation's live page, and is retained as verified; the charter figure is marked contested.

claims.text: The corporation's Citizen's Charter gives the fee for issue of a birth or death certificate as Rs. 20 per certificate, and the fee for supply of extra copies of a birth or death certificate as Rs. 20.
claims.notes: The charter's own service table, which names the AMOH as the officer rendering the service but does not state that this fee is confined to a counter channel; the counter-route scoping was an inference, not an observation of the source. Graded C because the document is twelve years past the revision date it states for itself. Marked contested on audit: it gives a different amount for the same output as the corporation's current page, which gives Rs. 45, and claim_hyderabad_birth_current_fee_and_timeframe_unknown records that whether this figure is still in force is not established by any reviewed public page.

claims.text: The corporation's Citizen's Charter gives a time frame of 7 days for issue of a birth or death certificate and 3 days for supply of extra copies of a birth or death certificate.
claims.notes: Service-level targets stated against the two rows that cover this scenario.

claims.text: The corporation's Citizen's Charter names the AMOH as the officer rendering the service for issue of a birth or death certificate and for supply of extra copies, and the DC as the officer to be contacted for delay or default in that service.
claims.notes: The charter's table carries a dedicated column for the officer to approach when the service is late or refused, which is a route to the deciding role rather than a general agency name.

claims.text: The corporation's Citizen's Charter gives the documents required for issue of a birth or death certificate, and for supply of extra copies, as an application in the prescribed format, under a table heading stating that all copies are to be attested by a Gazetted Officer.
claims.notes: The only entry in the documents column for these two rows is the application itself; no supporting document is named.

claims.text: The corporation's birth and death page states that certificates are issued instantly from Mee-Seva centres after approval by the Registrar or AMOH.
claims.notes: The timing figure covers the Mee-Seva counter step only and is expressly conditioned on prior approval by the Registrar or AMOH, for which no period is published. The intake sentence this record previously carried was split out on audit as claim_hyderabad_birth_meeseva_noninstitutional_intake; this record keeps its published identity under protocol section 1.

claims.text: The corporation's birth and death page states that for an institutional delivery the request comes through the hospital online to the Sub-Registrar or AMC, that hospitals enter the events online, and that after verification and approval by the Registrars of Births and Deaths citizens can take such certificates from Mee-Seva centres only.
claims.notes: A rule that decides which route applies according to where the birth took place.

claims.text: The corporation's birth and death page states that each hospital has to submit Form 1 for a birth, signed and stamped, to the corporation within 7 days from the date of occurrence of the event.
claims.notes: A duty on the hospital rather than on the family; recorded for the route and not used for the time cell, since hospital-side registration steps are outside this scenario.

claims.text: The corporation's birth and death page states that after approval by the Registrar or AMOH an SMS alert is sent to the citizen.
claims.notes: A surface the applicant sees after the decision is taken.

claims.text: The corporation's births and deaths portal publishes a birth certificate route reachable without login that takes an acknowledgement or application number and offers a search action.
claims.notes: The route's own field label and action were observed; no number was entered, so nothing is claimed about what it returns.

claims.text: The corporation's births and deaths portal serves a birth certificate layout headed 'BIRTH CERTIFICATE (Issued Under Section 12/17)' which recites that the information is taken from the original record of birth in the register for a named ward and circle of the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation, and which carries fields for name, gender, date of birth, place of birth, parents' names and registration number.
claims.notes: Identifies the document the citizen ends up with, and the statutory sections it is issued under.

claims.text: The corporation's application for a birth certificate asks for the circle or locality, the date of birth, the sex, the child's name, the father's name, the mother's name, the place of birth, the number of copies required, and whether the certificate is wanted by courier with a delivery name and address.
claims.notes: Particulars the applicant supplies on the form; the form names no supporting document to attach.

claims.text: The corporation's application for a birth certificate carries the note that the birth certificate will be issued subject to the entry being found registered with GHMC records.
claims.notes: The qualifying rule that matches this scenario's trigger, a birth already on the register.

claims.text: The Citizen's Charter published on the corporation's live homepage states on its face that it was prepared by the department on 10 May 2013 and would be revised on or before 13 May 2014.
claims.notes: Recorded because it is the document every fee, time frame and officer designation in this ledger's counter route depends on.

claims.text: The corporation's births and deaths portal offers a login using a password and an OTP sent to a registered mobile number, and that surface was not entered in this run.
claims.notes: Boundary statement, recorded as a limitation and not used to support any positive cell value. The certificate search route beside it needs no login, which is why the after-submission evidence does not rest on the gated surface.

claims.text: Whether the Rs. 20 fee and the 7-day and 3-day time frames the corporation's charter sets for its own counter route are still in force is not established by any reviewed public page, the charter being twelve years past its own stated revision date and no current corporation page restating them.
claims.notes: Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Not login-related.

claims.text: Which supporting documents a parent must produce at a Mee-Seva centre to obtain a copy of an already registered birth is not established by any reviewed public page; the corporation's page refers to 'all required documents' without naming them and its printable application form names none.
claims.notes: Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Not login-related.

claims.text: The corporation's birth and death page states that for a non-institutional birth the citizen approaches the Mee-Seva centre with all required documents including Form 1.
claims.notes: Split from claim_hyderabad_birth_meeseva_instant_issue on audit for atomicity. The documents are described only as 'all required documents including form-1', without a list, which is why the documents cell is mentioned rather than stated. This sentence describes intake for a birth not yet on the register and so sits at the edge of a scenario scoped to a birth already registered; it is retained because the corporation's page presents Mee-Seva intake and certificate issue as one counter flow, and because the only cell it supports is mentioned rather than stated.
